items.title: The Best Games Like GTA 6 to Play on PC in 2026
items.summary: Looking for open-world chaos without the wait? From Cyberpunk 2077 to indie gems like Shakedown: Hawaii, here are the best games like GTA 6.
items.content:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is set to be a titanic shift in gaming for a lot of people. However, it’s also going to cost a fair bit of cash, and its specific vibe might not be for everyone. Exploring a massive open world is a lot of fun, and GTA 6 certainly doesn’t have a monopoly on how you can go about it. Whether you’re looking to tide yourself over until you can justify the expense, or you simply want an open-world crime game with a different flavour, we’re going to help you out with the best games like GTA 6.

While there’s one very obvious answer on the list here, we’ve tried to keep things varied. There are plenty of fantastic open-world sandboxes available right now, and we can always spice things up with a few genre shifts and indie gems. Let’s get into the list.

Cyberpunk 2077 is a wildly different game from the one it was at launch. Night City is now a seamless open world filled with an absurd number of characters to talk to, weapons to master, and ways to approach every mission. With overhauled vehicle combat, fancier cyberware augments, and a world that’s eye-wateringly beautiful to explore, we’d argue that this is one of the best open-world RPGs ever made.

Saints Row IV is easily the silliest entry in the series. It puts you in the shoes of the President of the United States right as aliens invade Earth and trap humanity inside a virtual simulation. The bad news is, well, all of that. The good news is that being in a simulation means you get to unlock superpowers—some of which allow you to create tornadoes just by sprinting down the street. It’s also fully co-op, meaning you and a friend can enjoy the open-world chaos together.

This is the obvious pick if you haven’t played it yet and want a game that’s almost exactly like GTA 6 without actually being GTA 6. It lets you play as three distinct protagonists whose lives constantly intersect throughout a story packed with ups, downs, and plenty of anger. Alongside an incredible single-player sandbox in Los Santos, it also grants you access to GTA Online, which remains an unmatched multiplayer experience.

Watch_Dogs 2 is an absolute delight of an open-world adventure. You play as a hacker named Marcus, who uses a weaponised thunderball (basically a heavy-duty yo-yo) to knock people out and has a bone to pick with a corrupt tech CEO. Thankfully, you’re not alone; you’ll team up with the hacker collective DedSec to take down the system. It’s a vibrant, upbeat experience that lets you hack nearly anything in San Francisco in an instant, and it still looks stunning today.

If you’ve ever wanted to play GTA set in Hong Kong, then Sleeping Dogs is the game for you. It places a much heavier focus on martial arts combat than GTA does, delivering a constant string of cinematic set pieces as you try to take down a massive Triad organisation from within as an undercover cop. This is a tense, brutal crime drama set in a gorgeous world filled with plenty of distractions alongside hard-hitting story moments.

We’re moving into the indie section of this list now, so please enjoy. Tiny Terry’s Turbo Trip is an absurdist, charming take on the open-world city game. Your main goal is to launch yourself into space in your car, and you’ll do whatever it takes to accomplish that. You can run around committing petty crimes, stealing turbo junk, crashing into townsfolk, and gliding around town while being a general menace.

Retro City Rampage DX is, in essence, an 8-bit demake of a classic GTA game packed with homages to countless retro titles and pop culture icons. This leans much closer to an unhinged arcade game, really, but it’s an absolute blast to play. If you want the chaotic vibes of GTA in bite-sized chunks—complete with cardboard boxes to hide in and high-speed police chases—you’ll adore this.

From the creators of Retro City Rampage, Shakedown: Hawaii is all about building a “very reasonable” corporate empire in a 16-bit open world. You’re just looking to make some money, and sometimes that means shaking down local shops, extorting businesses, or resorting to over-the-top violence—all in the name of legitimate enterprise. It feels like a classic top-down GTA game lost in time, and it’s endlessly entertaining in how bombastic it is.

Jason likes to focus on roguelikes and co-op games; in a dream world he'd make a living writing about Dark Souls. As well as being a writer he also does personal training and accounting and can occasionally be seen on other people's streams. Being a big fan of fluffy things means he has two cats, both of whom refuse to let him sleep, but at least they are cute.

Cyberpunk 2077 Multiplayer Might Become a Reality, But Not in the Way Fans Expected
items.summary: One of the biggest fan projects for Cyberpunk 2077 is now in open beta, allowing players to join up together in long awaited multiplayer.
items.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One of the biggest fan projects for Cyberpunk 2077 has finally entered open beta, setting up online multiplayer for the first time in the CD Projekt Red developed open-world RPG. The first-person action of Night City is expanding in full force to support a server’s-worth of players, allowing them to get together to explore the setting or complete missions together. Called “ CyberMP ,” this six-year modding endeavor is dropping at the perfect time, as Cyberpunk 2077 ‘s original developers are taking more and more interest at the direction of fan-made content while creating their next big titles.

With a trailer released on November 15, 2026, the CyberMP project has officially made both a client and server players can access freely to start testing the mod. Obviously, players need to have a copy of Cyberpunk 2077 downloaded on PC in order to access the multiplayer mod, but once they do, it is very reminiscent of something like GTA Online . While far from complete and not without problems, this fulfills an original ambition from CD Projekt Red that had to be scrapped due to the disastrous launch of Cyberpunk 2077 and all the time it took for the game to get on the right track.

CyberMP is truly a multiplayer mod that has it all, hosting servers where vast amounts of players can jump into Night City together at the same time. In the words of the modders, “no invites or applications needed,” so players can jump in once they visit the project’s website and download/install the appropriate files. Unfortunately, crashes, server drops, stuttering, and other performance issues make the mod’s beta far from ideal, but the team behind CyberMP is eager to implement fixes fast. Some of the content players can expect from this Cyberpunk 2077 mod include:

Players can race each other using the vehicles they unlock, or steal the right weapons to duel each other in select spaces. From the limited mod gameplay players have explored so far, every character you encounter has a yellow health bar, along with an abbreviated version of their user name (again, similar to GTA Online ). There seems to be no limit to the amount of players in a select server, leading to cooperation in some environments, and complete pandemonium in others. The PvP servers seem to encourage a smaller crop of players, were others can find and challenge each other naturally to see whose build is better.

For one of the best selling open-world games right now on Steam, this is a huge expansion to what is possible in Cyberpunk 2077 , even if limited right now. The team behind CyberMP is currently prioritizing fixing the performance of the mod, making sure crashes are less frequent and seeing how the project works when real players arrive in big numbers. Thankfully, the long development time for this mod also confirms no “vibe-based” gen-AI coding was used, adding an authenticity to the mod around 90% of others for Cyberpunk 2077 don’t have right now.

One of the most fascinating details about CyberMP is that it is completing an original vision for Cyberpunk 2077 that CD Projekt Red wasn’t able to do. At first, CD Projekt Red had planned to make a multiplayer mode for Cyberpunk 2077 a top priority for the game post-launch, before that idea was cancelled in favor of fixing the many, many problems of the title when it came out. CD Projekt Red’s countless updates over time eventually course-corrected Cyberpunk 2077 heavily, culminating in the celebrated Phantom Liberty expansion, which established the “definitive” version of the game players are the most used to.

Another AAA project set in Cyberpunk 2077 ‘s world was planned to have online multiplayer with CD Projekt Red too, but that was also cancelled. This was due to the fact that the developer decided to move forward with other big projects instead, such as The Witcher 4 , a new expansion for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt , and early steps for a Cyberpunk sequel. As a result, CyberMP is almost like a correction of the past, with fans making something that may have resembled an official direction the game might have gone in under different circumstances.

While some studios might search to stomp out a fan project that creates something they were unable to do, CD Projekt Red has embraced its modding community openly. Much like Bethesda, Rockstar, and other companies, CD Projekt Red has seen the value in fan ideas, which can often be inventive enough to inspire official game design choices on other titles down the line. To that point, CD Projekt Red has actually hired several prominent modders from games like Cyberpunk 2077 or The Witcher 3 to officially join the development team, with a large portion of some groups made up of former mod creators.

It’s entirely possible that the success of the CyberMP mod may lead to CD Projekt Red reaching out, not to disable the multiplayer servers, but to recruit those involved. By doing this, the studio may have an even better chance to accomplish their original goal, which was to have multiplayer elements in Night City to begin with. Bringing online to each of their games seems to be a big goal of CD Projekt Red, so having a Cyberpunk 2077 mod with that concept to go off of could be a huge source of inspiration for the game’s sequel in the years to come.

What excites you the most about a multiplayer mod for Cyberpunk 2077 ? Let us know in the comments below!

10 Open-World Games Better Than Elden Ring in 2026
items.summary: Elden Ring is a fantastic game, but open-world games like The Witcher 3 are even better.
items.content:
Image via FromSoftware Add CBR on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By George Chrysostomou Published Nov 16, 2026, 10:30 PM EST George is an experienced entertainment and creative writer and a politics fan. If he's not talking about the latest MCU release, he's probably focused on local by-elections. With a love for analyzing detailed character work and a penchant for speculating on the upcoming twists and turns of major franchises, George is ultimately fascinated by the creative process. Sign in to your CBR account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread 6 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Elden Ring quickly became one of the most popular open-world games of all time when it was released in 2022. Four years later, in 2026, many gamers still consider it to be the best game in the genre, but there are a few open-world games, like Ghost of Yōtei , that arguably surpass it.

There's no denying that Elden Ring is an incredible game, but it's not for everyone due to its challenging combat and a story that's told more through lore than a traditional narrative. Open-world games like The Witcher 3 have stronger narratives, and other games give players more freedom, which is why they're the best games in the genre today.

Red Dead REdemption 2 screenshot showing Arthur on a horse riding through a mostly empty Western town Image via Rockstar Red Dead Redemption 2 gets plenty of attention, but its reputation is well earned. Once players get through its slower opening, they're free to explore a sprawling Wild West inspired by real history and locations. Rockstar fills that world with small details and dynamic encounters, designed to make it feel unusually alive.

Like Elden Ring , Red Dead Redemption 2 rewards players who wander off the beaten path, with countless hidden secrets and unexpected encounters waiting to be discovered. Where RDR2 has the advantage is in its commitment to realism. Combined with its accessible gunplay, those systems create a level of immersion that few open-world games can match.

Image via Sucker Punch Ghost of Tsushima was already one of the strongest open-world games of its generation, and Ghost of Yōtei builds on nearly everything that made it work. The sequel expands the formula with a more flexible approach to exploration and combat, creating another immersive experience that rarely forces players down a single path.

Where Ghost of Yōtei really pulls ahead of Elden Ring is in its character-driven storytelling. Atsu's journey gives the adventure a more personal emotional core. It also offers surprisingly precise combat, which makes switching between weapons feel fast and satisfying.It's remarkably easy to get lost in Ghost of Yōtei 's world.

Image via CD Projekt Red The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt and Elden Ring are often compared, and for good reason. Both rank among the best fantasy open-world games ever made , with memorable bosses and plenty of freedom to explore. Where The Witcher 3 has the clear advantage, though, is in its storytelling.

Open-world games like Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 are the best games of their kind.

Geralt may look like a typical gruff fantasy anti-hero, but The Witcher 3 gives him, Ciri, Yennefer, and the rest of the game's supporting cast far more emotional depth than players might expect. Its strongest moments work because the relationships feel personal. Elden Ring excels at environmental storytelling, but The Witcher 3 delivers a more character-driven experience.

Image via Insomniac Games The first Spider-Man game from Insomniac Games was a stunning reimagining of the superhero world and a testament to Marvel's most popular character. The Miles Morales spinoff was equally exceptional, adding further depth to Miles Morales. Spider-Man 2 is the perfect follow-up, and while it might be underrated by fans, it's a more complete experience than Elden Ring .

Much could be said about the way the game tackles Peter's personal relationships and the famous Venom arc. Even more could be discussed surrounding the improved web-slinging mechanics and the flow of combat. What really deserves praise, however, is the seamless way this open-world title portrays a duo of leading heroes, giving ample time and energy to each.

items.title: Ever wanted to play a multiplayer version of Cyberpunk 2077 with your friends? Well, thanks to a mod now in beta, you can
items.summary: "After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," says the dev.
items.content:
Image credit: Eurogamer/CyberMP News by Dom Peppiatt Deputy Editorial Director Published on Nov. 16, 2026, 2:19 p.m. 4 comments Follow Cyberpunk 2077 Prioritise us on Google You may have recently read that CD Projekt Red's in-development Cyberpunk 2 may be trying to revive the original game's online ambitions . But, if you don't want to wait the many years it'll likely be before the Cyberpunk 2077 sequel arrives, then I've got good news for you: Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta.

"After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders on the CyberMP Discord channel wrote (thanks RPS ). "Anyone can jump in and play now - no invites or applications needed." The team notes, however, that this is "true beta", meaning "Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers."

Alongside the potential shakiness, the devs say it's also possible the mod could ping your anti-virus software, since it "doesn't have a digital signature yet". Whilst the priorities for the team lie in "polishing the foundations" and "fixing crashes and stability", more features are eventually planned. But for now, they stress, "let's see how the project handles real player traffic!"

So, what exactly is it? CyberMP is a dedicated multiplayer modification for Cyberpunk 2077 that allows you and your friends to explore Night City together: drive vehicles, engage in combat, and play custom community-created game modes on high-tick dedicated servers. You need an official copy of the game to play it (obviously), and the mod is completely free to download. You can download the mod, and read a fair amount of how to get it working, what to expect from it, and how to troubleshoot any issues, over at its dedicated website.

If you're thinking 'Hang on, why does Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer sound so familiar?', it's because the game was supposed to receive an official multiplayer mode after its original release. Thanks to its shaky launch, however, plans changed, and CD Projekt Red later announced that multiplayer would be a separate "triple-A release" , but, eventually, that too was cancelled. The studio is still keen to honour the idea, though, and recently stated it's "focusing on bringing online into all of our franchises one day" .

This isn't the first big bit of news we've had about Cyberpunk 2077 mods this week. Just yesterday, a new mod called 'Torrent' added 3D rain, lightning storms, and tyre spray to Night City - all rendered and made lovely with a new lighting system that seems to play nicely with other weather mods that have been created for the game.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Multiplayer Finally Goes Live
items.content:
Cyberpunk 2077 game cover Add ScreenRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Tom Wilson Published Nov 16, 2026, 6:32 AM EST Tom Wilson is a Gaming Features Writer at Screen Rant. Over the past five years, Tom has worked as the Editor-in-Chief at The Game Crater, as a Staff Writer for GamingIntel, a List Writer at TheGamer, and, of course, as a Senior Writer at ScreenRant. Tom has experience writing reviews, guides, news, and features, and has been responsible for teams of writers, training them and editing their work. Tom graduated with a Masters in Multimedia Journalism, and has since gone on to build up his portfolio of games journalism work. Sign in to your ScreenRant account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Cyberpunk 2077 is the game that keeps on growing. CD Projekt Red, six years after the base game dropped, has released numerous updates of varying significance, as well as the critically acclaimed expansion and assorted expanded media releases. There is simply no shortage of ways to interact with Night City and the wider Cyberpunk world, unless you want to do so with a friend, of course. Cyberpunk 2077's official multiplayer was canceled back in 2021, with CD Projekt Red stating there are no plans to implement it in the future.

Naturally, this proved to be a huge blow to the game's fanbase, who had dreamed of roaming through Night City with their friends. However, it also proved to be a challenge for modders, who have since set about implementing what CD Projekt Red lacked the resources and time for. We've gotten announcements of a Far Cry -esque Cyberpunk 2077 co-op mod that makes the entire game's story playable with a friend, as well as a full-blown multiplayer experience which has finally gone live.

CyberMP is a mod that has been in the works for years. Its goal has always been to bring multiplayer to the streets of Night City and give players complete freedom over what that looks like. Offering the ability to create one's own server, CyberMP gives hosts control over almost every element of their version of Night City, including NPCs, world events, rules, economy, and more. It's impressive and has the potential to lead to complete reinventions of the core gameplay loop of Cyberpunk 2077 , much in the same way GTA Online does for GTA V .

CyberMP currently allows players to engage in PvP warfare, street races, and roleplaying, all of which are synchronized perfectly across each user's copy of the game. So, cars, unique player outfits, and every action will be seen simultaneously. This is made possible through fast network code as well as Easy Anti-Cheat, which prevents malicious actors from disrupting the server and ruining everyone's experience.

There are plans to add additional features and functions to CyberMP over the coming months, including proximity chat, which would allow for a greater degree of roleplaying potential. Currently, you can download the client from the mod's official website to join existing servers or host your own. It is in its Beta form, so prospective players should expect a myriad of bugs and missing features. However, for the most part, this is the intended CyberMP experience, offering a suite of impressive multiplayer features within Cyberpunk 2077 for the very first time.

It is worth noting that CyberMP is only available for the PC version of Cyberpunk 2077 .

Additionally, CyberMP has been designed with modders in mind, ensuring that the project can be expanded upon by anyone, thus making the possibilities for new features ostensibly endless. It's an exciting addition to the pantheon of amazing Cyberpunk 2077 mods , and a must-have for anyone who's been eagerly anticipating the day that the game finally gets its long-overdue multiplayer offering. Considering just how expansive Cyberpunk 2077's roleplaying options were before CyberMP's launch, fans are undoubtedly in for a world of new and exciting possibilities.

items.content:
Thought you were done with Night City? Well, Night City's not quite done with you!

Patch notes for Cyberpunk 2077's Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) are now available for your early perusal before the update hits the streets on October 22nd. Watch the Features Overview video to see some of the new features in action:

And if you want to know even more, read through the list of most important changes below:

Edgerunners Content

  • Added a new side quest, Clampdown, set before the events of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2. To unlock it, complete The Heist and two gigs for Wakako, then wait for a message from her.

    [/*]

  • Added a new 5-piece gear set based on the character King, which can be obtained during the Clampdown side quest.

    [/*]

  • Added a new radio station, HKGN 102.0 FM, featuring a selection of tracks from the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners series.

    [/*]

Show Off

  • A brand-new clothing collection has arrived in Night City! 5 new outfit sets can now be purchased from certain clothing vendors:

    • Maxiwear: available in Heywood, Arroyo, Little China

      [/*]

    • Jinguji: available in City Center

      [/*]

    • NetWatch: available in Kabuki, Japantown

      [/*]

    • IconAmerica: available in Pacifica, Badlands, Northside

      [/*]

    • And one more set that will hit Night City shelves just a little later...

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • The NUS Infiltrator clothing set can be now purchased from clothing vendors in Kabuki and Japantown.

    [/*]

  • 4 new TWINTONE skins for Quadra Turbo-R V-Tech are now available via Twitch Drops.

    [/*]

  • Some of the hairstyles that were previously exclusive to NPCs are now available for V. Please note that some hairstyles are available only to feminine or masculine body types.

    [/*]

  • Show off your chrome! You can now customize your hand cyberware. Equip your Mantis Blades, Gorilla Arms, Monowire or Projectile Launch System, and visit one of 5 Glamdocs (marked with a spray paint icon on the map) to give your implants a fresh, new look. Each Glamdoc is located in a unique shop, along with their own intro scene with voiceover and animations, and offers a unique catalog of cyberware skins with customizable colors.

    [/*]

  • Sometimes one gun just isn't enough. The new Double Trouble perk in the Cool tree (along with four auxiliary perks) introduces an entirely new playstyle, allowing you to dual-wield Pistols and Revolvers from the Power category.

    [/*]

  • Added frames from the Cyberpunk Trading Card Game to Photo Mode, allowing you to make your preem shots look like custom cards.

    [/*]

  • Added new poses in Photo Mode to show off your dual-wielding prowess.

    [/*]

Mod the World

Added Cross-Platform Mod Support, powered by mod.io, a first step into cross-platform modding that allows you to easily browse and install a selection of player-created mods directly from the in-game menu. More mods will become available over time. The feature is available on PC, Mac, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S.

Upgrading the World

  • Welcome to Paradise! Added a new side quest that takes you on a journey to uncover a mystery and explore Night City on a guided tour narrated by Richard Night. It unlocks after completing The Heist and reaching level 15 Street Cred.

    [/*]

  • Added 12 new Minor Arcana Tarot Cards to discover across Night City. The Tarot menu now has separate sections for Major and Minor Arcana. The new tarot cards are part of a new side quest, an extension of Fool on the Hill, which activates after scanning any of the new cards. Collect them all to get a special reward.

    [/*]

Quality of Life

  • Saves in the “Load Game” menu are now grouped by separate playthroughs.

    [/*]

  • Added item filters to apartment and vehicle stashes.

    [/*]

  • Modded saves in the "Load Game" menu are now marked with a dedicated icon. Please note that achievements and trophies cannot be earned while playing on console from a modded save file.

    [/*]

  • Updated the selection of AMD FSR options. FSR 3 upscaling is no longer included, while FSR 2.1, FSR 4, and FSR 3.1 Frame Generation remain available.

    [/*]

  • Updated the CD PROJEKT RED Account connection, My Rewards and telemetry consent menus.

    [/*]

Technology

  • Added support for DLSS 4.5, including up to 6X Multi Frame Generation or Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, and the 2nd Generation Transformer Model.

    [/*]

  • Added support for glasses-free 3D effects on compatible Samsung Odyssey 3D monitors, along with a Motion Comfort setting that lets you balance 3D depth and viewing comfort.

    [/*]

  • Added support for MetalFX Frame Interpolation on Mac.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle in settings for FSR Anti-Lag 2.

    [/*]

  • Introduced various performance optimizations, including improvements specifically for Ray Tracing.

    [/*]

  • Improved HDR rendering to provide more accurate colors, brightness, and contrast on compatible displays.

    [/*]

Fixes

  • Things Done Changed- Fixed an issue where the Delamain cab could get stuck after crashing into another vehicle, blocking quest progression.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where enabling Film Grain had no effect.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where tagging enemies while scanning could also cause V to crouch or stand up when using certain control schemes.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where controller settings for the Third-Person Camera were missing.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several typos in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added various other fixes for features and content introduced since Patch 2.1.

    [/*]

items.content:
To survive in Night City, you need someone to watch your back. On the way to the major leagues, V managed to gather a remarkable crew. You could even say, a crew to remember!

From trusted allies to unforgettable personalities, these are the people who helped shape V’s journey through the City of Dreams. This episode of It’s All About You is dedicated to the legendary crew that stood by V through every high and low.

Thank you for staying with us and expressing your love for Cyberpunk 2077 in the most creative ways possible. Don’t forget to check out our gallery to see more works, and, of course, share your creations with us: http://cdpred.ly/AAY

See you in the next episode!

items.content:
Listen up, Samurai! 🤘🔥

Celebrate five years of Cyberpunk 2077 in this special anniversary episode of It’s All About You, looking back on Night City’s unforgettable stories through the legends and music you met along your journey!

Sure, the city’s full of noise — sirens, synths, gunfire in the distance — but if there’s one song that became its soul, it’s “Never Fade Away.”

We brought together legendary artists from across the city of dreams to reinterpret this iconic track — each in their own voice, their own style, their own rebellion. ❤️‍🔥

Plug in, turn it up, and dive into our latest It’s All About You episode.

Because legends don’t fade.
